newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan to unveil new economic resources.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan to unveil new economic resources.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Thursday he would unveil new resources to close big fiscal and trade deficits next week.

"The studies on the second resource package were finalised at the cabinet meeting yesterday. We will give our nation the good news about the second resource package early next week," Erbakan told reporters.
"Thus we will increase exports, set up foreign trade balance and narrow deficits," he said.
Erbakan did not give any further details but State Minister Abdullah Gul, also the government spokesman, said late on Wednesday the new package would raise $10 billion.
Officials say it may include new plans for privatisation and securitisation of state real estates.

Erbakan's first resource package, unveiled in late July, included issuing foreign currency denominated bonds, sale of state properties, incentives and tax exemptions for Turkish workers abroad to attract their savings into the country, and a central cash management for the public sector.
He says the first package will raise some $10 billion in three years, a target that economists say is not realistic.
